speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I presented the Solidarity Budget in this House seven weeks ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More people are expected to be infected as countries come to grips with what it takes to contain this virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lockdowns and movement restrictions have exerted a huge cost, with major job losses in many economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the highest level since the Great Depression.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New jobless claims also continue to be high in May.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Eurozone economy is estimated to have contracted 3.8% in the first quarter of 2020 – its sharpest decline on record.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The IMF has predicted that Asia will see zero growth in 2020 – the worst growth performance in 60 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In some countries, bitter differences over how to deal with the pandemic have deepened societal fault lines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key uncertainty arises from the virus itself.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is still much that we do not know about COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, what is the risk of transmission by asymptomatic carriers?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Are recovered patients immune to future infections and if so, for how long?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also uncertain how the pandemic will evolve in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Will there be significant mutations of the virus?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Will there be a resurgence in infections as restrictions on activities and travel are gradually lifted around the world?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is a wide range of views among experts – from five months to beyond 18 months for a viable vaccine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Making the vaccine available globally will also be a huge challenge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The situation is fast-evolving and global efforts at containing the pandemic are uneven and uncoordinated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These uncertainties affect whether and when countries will be able to contain the pandemic successfully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In turn, this affects how far and how fast the global economy can recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small open economy, Singapore's economic outlook depends critically on the state of the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With COVID-19, the global outlook depends on how the global community is able to contain the outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Outward-oriented sectors such as manufacturing, wholesale trade and transportation and storage have been affected by both weak external demand and supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The circuit breaker, which was put in place to bring down community transmission decisively, also affected many businesses that could not operate offsite.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As announced by the Multi-Ministry Task Force on 19 May, we are preparing to reopen the economy in three phases, guided by public health considerations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we open up progressively, we will continue to give more support to businesses which are not yet ready to reopen and workers who are still unable to resume work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key is to reopen safely and this needs to be done carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we have learnt from the experience of other countries, life will not return to what it was before COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we reopen and have more activities and interactions, we are likely to see a rise in community cases.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must therefore be psychologically prepared for setbacks before we safely transition to a new normal and build a COVID-safe nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the coming months as we transition to the next phase, many of our precautionary measures will remain in place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The global economy is unlikely to recover quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be prepared for tough times in the months ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a challenge for this generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a test of our strength and fortitude, a test of our resilience and unity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How we respond will define us as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The past few months, especially the circuit breaker, have been tough for everyone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have lost their jobs or suffered pay cuts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mid-career Singaporeans who support both their children and elderly parents are anxious about job stability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses are concerned about cash flow and staying afloat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Families have found it challenging to balance working from home and adapting to home-based learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has also hit the vulnerable groups in the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have seen more families seeking counselling for marital conflicts and family violence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our path forward will be tough, but we will journey together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, I will introduce this $33 billion Supplementary Budget for the next phase of our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The central focus of this Budget is jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget will continue to support workers and businesses who remain affected by border closures and safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the significant changes in the global economy ahead, we will provide support to enable our businesses and workers to adapt, transform and seize new opportunities – to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We aim to enable workers and businesses to go through this difficult period together in a synergistic way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also provide additional support to our households and community to cope with the disruptions and seize new opportunities in adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help us build a stronger and more inclusive society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide funding to frontline agencies to continue our fight against the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will boost our clinical management of cases and our swabbing and testing capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The coming months will test our resolve as a society and as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will need to adapt and stay resolute and resilient amidst a rapidly evolving, uncertain situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In that light, I have decided to call this the Fortitude Budget – courage in adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a landmark package and a necessary response to an unprecedented crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A distinctive feature of this Budget is that we are setting aside a bigger contingent sum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are dealing with unprecedented uncertainty across all fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A bigger contingent sum will allow us to respond swiftly to fast-changing situations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before I get into the details, I thank our partners – NTUC, Singapore Business Federation, Future Economy Council members, Emerging Stronger Task Force members, social sector agency partners and leaders, and many citizens and groups who have given us very useful feedback.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank my team in MOF who has been working non-stop since our first Unity Budget this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The central focus of this Budget is jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Large parts of the last three Budgets were directed at protecting the livelihoods of our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Budget, we will do even more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, over 140,000 enterprises employ 1.9 million local employees across various industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these enterprises are facing not only immediate challenges but also structural challenges that threaten their survival.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of our workers will lose their jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of these jobs will not come back.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other jobs will look different going into the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we navigate through the current storm, we must stay on course and set our direction right to prevail over the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The tripartite structure that has served Singapore so well over the years will need to be reinforced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses need to adapt and transform and workers need to adapt and re-skill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You have my assurance that the Government will provide strong support to bring all parties together to navigate through these turbulent waters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will cover three inter-related subjects in three parts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, how we provide timely support to businesses and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, how we support businesses to transform to secure the future of our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, how we will help Singaporeans upskill and re-skill to seize opportunities now and in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses have been hard-hit by the simultaneous demand and supply shocks caused by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I had a virtual meeting with the Singapore Business Federation and the Future Economy Council members and Emerging Stronger Task Force co-chiars last week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While businesses appreciated the support over the past three Budgets, they recognised that the Government cannot carry businesses indefinitely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses are trying hard to get back on their feet and reopen safely as they emerge from the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are fully behind them and will further strengthen our support for businesses on the 3Cs – cash flow, costs and credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will help businesses on the first "C", cash flow, through the Jobs Support Scheme, or JSS, which supports firms in retaining and paying their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the circuit breaker was imposed, I increased the wage support under the JSS to 75% of the first $4,600 of wages in April for every local employee.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the circuit breaker was extended in May, I extended the higher level of support to May.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is because most firms had to either stop operating or operate at a much-reduced level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The temporary increase in support was planned for only two months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To provide additional relief for firms as they safely re-open after the circuit breaker period, I will provide an additional month of support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be computed based on the wages paid in August 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This support will be at the same levels as those provided during the non-circuit breaker months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms will receive this additional month of support in the October 2020 JSS payout.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second enhancement is for firms that cannot resume operations immediately after the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For such firms, I will continue providing wage support at 75% until August 2020 or when they are allowed to re-open, whichever is earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes retail outlets, gym and fitness studios and cinemas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third enhancement is to refine the classification of firms in the different JSS tiers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in the aerospace sector, including those in Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul, will now receive 75% wage support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The full list of eligible sectors and the qualifying criteria are in the Annex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible firms will receive a back-payment to top up their previous JSS payouts to the higher level of support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This retrospective payment will be made by July.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the built environment sector, which includes construction, we will raise the wage support to 75%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This sector will be affected by the phased and gradual resumption of activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This 75% support will only apply to wages paid between June and August.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge leaders in our industries to use this additional cushion to retain your staff, speed up adaptation, and move towards a viable business model.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Please make full use of the schemes available to train workers and upgrade your corporate capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened that some firms which have not been as badly affected by the pandemic have returned or donated their JSS payouts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage other firms that are able, to do so as well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide support to businesses for the second "C", costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the circuit breaker period, we provided a Foreign Worker Levy waiver and rebate to support businesses employing migrant workers that had to suspend operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some businesses will not be allowed to resume operations on-site immediately after the circuit breaker is lifted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will extend the Foreign Worker Levy waiver and rebate for up to two months for such businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will include all businesses in the construction, marine and offshore and process sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The waiver will be 100% in June, and 50% in July.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rebate will be $750 in June and $375 in July.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The CPF Transition Offset scheme will similarly be deferred until after the higher contribution rates take effect.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses have also given feedback that while the JSS provides support on wage costs, they are facing difficulties with rental costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given that businesses will need more time and support to get back on their feet post-circuit breaker, we will now do more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will significantly add to the support for rental costs earlier provided through the Property Tax Rebate for 2020 in the Unity and Resilience Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also expect landlords to do something, and that will be legislated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will provide a cash grant to offset the rental costs of SME tenants, to be disbursed through property owners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together with the Property Tax Rebate, the Government will, in effect, offset about two months of rental for qualifying SME tenants of commercial properties, and about one month for qualifying SME tenants of industrial and office properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The grant will be disbursed automatically to property owners from end-July.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, the Minister for Law will introduce a new Bill next week.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will mandate that landlords contribute by granting a rental waiver to their SME tenants who have suffered a significant revenue drop in the past few months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government does not ordinarily intervene in contracts after they have been entered into.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, as the Minister for Law had explained in his Second Reading speech on the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill, in exceptional situations, such as this, the Government needs to intervene, through legislation, with temporary targeted steps to safeguard the economic structure for the common good.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The new Bill will also cover provisions on temporary relief from onerous contractual terms, such as excessive late payment interest or charges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will also allow tenants to repay their arrears through instalments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other SME tenants in industrial and office properties will also be given some relief.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMEs also already benefit from temporary relief from rental payment obligations till October.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, these will provide substantial support on rental costs, for our SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will also continue to lead by example in supporting our tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide two more months of rental waivers for commercial tenants and hawkers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The total rental waiver will now be four months for commercial tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Stallholders in hawker centres and markets managed by Government agencies will get a total of five months of rental waivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For industrial, office, and agricultural tenants of Government agencies, I will provide one more month of rental waiver.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will now receive a total of two months of rental waiver.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also ensure that these measures flow through to help sub-tenants, many of whom are SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will dovetail with measures for SMEs being studied by the Minister for Law.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We introduced and enhanced various financing schemes, such as the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the Enterprise Financing Scheme in the past Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The schemes have catalysed $4.5 billion of loans so far, benefiting 5,000 businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is more than three times the amount of loans catalysed for the whole of 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MAS, together with banks, finance companies and insurers, has also introduced relief measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These help individuals and SMEs to continue servicing their loans and paying for insurance coverage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Notwithstanding this enhanced support, business leaders, including at my virtual meeting with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and the Future Economy Council, tell me that in this environment, some promising start-ups in Singapore are finding it hard to raise capital and develop their businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Left unaddressed, this could set back our efforts and result in the loss of good jobs and good companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is important to preserve what has been built up in our innovation eco-system so painstakingly over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To bridge this financing gap, I will provide financing support for promising start-ups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These start-ups can also make full use of the SGUnited Traineeship scheme, which I will cover later, to bring in graduating students with deep interests in the fields they are exploring and build up our talent base.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are many significant infrastructure projects, including public infrastructure, such as MRT lines and public housing that we must continue to plan and build.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered the higher tier of JSS support for locals who are in the sector, including project managers, engineers, architects, draughtsman and quantity surveyors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have also covered the Foreign Worker Levy rebate and waiver to support businesses in this sector, so that they can continue to play their part in building Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will now provide support to co-share the additional costs that will be incurred by businesses who will need to meet additional requirements in order to resume their existing projects safely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for National Development and BCA will announce the details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, our support in past Budgets and this Fortitude Budget will help tide businesses through their periods of closure and to retain and rebuild core capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This support would enable most sectors to recover in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But some sectors, such as aviation and tourism, will take longer to re-open fully, given the restrictions on global travel for the foreseeable future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will consider providing additional help, depending on the situation and longer term shape of these industries and plans for the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the interim, I urge businesses to make good use of the existing support and consider how to transform for a post-COVID world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered the support that we are providing to businesses in the near term, to save jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ensure good job opportunities remain available for Singaporeans, we must work to build strong and viable businesses for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce to plan for the post-COVID world to study how we can emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Emerging Stronger Taskforce will work with the Future Economy Council Sub-Committees to study how sectors can adjust to the many changes that are coming.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will draw on support from industry experts and consultancy firms to come up with actionable recommendations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the sectors that are more badly hit, and which also face significant structural disruptions, we will undertake a review on the medium-term outlook and our responses to adapt to the changes ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After observing companies for several years now since we started work on the Future Economy, I found that companies that are adapting to structural changes early are also adapting better to this sudden shock.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If change is a constant, innovation and resilience are simply manifestations of our ability to deal with change – be it persistent or sudden.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Emerging Stronger Task Force is studying two key shifts: the rise of digital transformation and the decline in support for globalisation; and shifts in global supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These shifts were already taking place, but COVID-19 has accelerated them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our businesses must adapt and we will support them in this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building on the momentum of digital transformation, the first key shift is in the digital transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will not go back to our old ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digital solutions will become more deeply embedded in our lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Telecommuting, online food and services, and virtual events are now the norm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A McKinsey study shows that we have seen the equivalent of five years of consumer and business digital adoption in just eight weeks since the COVID-19 pandemic started.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, COVID-19 has done what many CEOs and CTOs found hard to do – accelerate digitalisation!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I know that many businesses fear being left behind and shut out of the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses that are not digitally connected have been hit hard during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Earlier, we had been supporting businesses strongly to go digital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that businesses are now taking this seriously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those who are willing to transform will not be left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our augmented support for digital transformation in this Budget has three groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, for those who have not begun using digital tools, we will help them to get on board with digital transformation, building on current momentum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, in e-payments, the take-up by businesses has risen sharply – 50,000 more businesses have adopted PayNow Corporate since April this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They should not be left behind as the whole economy transforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will enhance our support for businesses which are ready to take their basic payment and invoicing functions digital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be coupled with support to keep their business running and even acquire new revenue lines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will help businesses to implement safe management measures and business continuity strategies to adapt to new post-COVID norms, an area that the Singapore Business Federation suggested supporting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We had earlier enhanced SMEs Go Digital to help businesses adopt digital solutions to cope with circuit breaker measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under SMEs Go Digital, we have rolled out the Food Delivery and e-commerce Booster Packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than 10,000 food services and retail establishments have benefited from these packages and gone online.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will start with the F&B and retail sectors, which are most affected by the safe distancing requirements as we re-open the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, businesses which already have basic digital capabilities, should deepen their digital transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will help them make use of advanced digital tools in an integrated way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, developing Offline-to-Online business models to access new domestic revenue streams and international demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from businesses, our schools and Institutes of Higher Learning must also make full use of digital technologies for learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOE has been doing this from the time I was Education Minister.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Student Learning Space (SLS), designed as a platform for self-directed learning, has been instrumental in supporting our teachers for home-based learning during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will harness the talents of our best software engineers, AI experts, learning scientists and educators to develop the relevant pedagogy and build new digital platforms for online teaching and learning, and integrate the latest advancements in AI and learning sciences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Research Foundation and MOE will provide more details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are committing our fullest support to help our businesses ride the wave of digital transformation and technological changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But success will require strong partnerships across the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To catalyse partnerships, we will introduce a set of National Innovation Challenges, riding on the success of the Open Innovation Platform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the National Innovation Challenges, we will focus on partnerships to develop industry-led solutions to the challenges that all businesses are grappling with: starting with how we can reopen Singapore safely – to achieve safe workplaces, safe homes, safe schools and safe commuting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The relevant agencies will articulate the critical problems that we seek to solve, or the leap that we are hoping to make.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope that corporates, start-ups and others in the private and people sectors can step forward to form partnerships to provide solutions that can be scaled.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will provide support for this innovation drive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Research Foundation and the Ministers for Communications and Information and for Trade and Industry will share more details on these initiatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has also accelerated the decline in support for globalisation and disrupted supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this new world, we must continue to build on our reputation as a trusted, neutral, and reliable Global-Asia node.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last month, Singapore issued a Joint Ministerial Statement alongside 10 other countries affirming our commitment to upholding supply chain connectivity and resilience during the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These links will support our businesses to go digital and global.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By staying successful, they will create good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, in the Networked Trade Platform, we have set up customs declaration data exchanges with countries in the region and further afield, such as Australia, China and the Netherlands to facilitate trade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Grow Digital programme is also helping SMEs to access overseas markets through e-commerce platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken on the first two thrusts – providing timely support for our businesses, and accelerating transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By supporting our businesses to stay viable, they save jobs and also create good jobs for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I now turn to the third thrust, on supporting our workers to secure these opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An adaptable and skilled workforce will in turn power our businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a synergy that we must seek to achieve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the tough months ahead, we must be prepared for some job losses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we will try to preserve jobs in the midst of this crisis, we cannot protect every job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, you have my assurance that the Government will protect every worker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as you are willing to pick up new skills and adapt, to access available opportunities to work or learn, the Government will provide our strongest support to help you.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have built up a strong base of support to help workers train and get good jobs, especially in sectors with growth potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Unity Budget, I announced enhancements, in the form of the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also enhanced our placement and training programmes in the Unity and Resilience Budgets, to boost support for our workers in sectors that were more severely impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will support the immediate needs of our workers and raise the skills of our people for future jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, these cater to workers with different skill levels and career aspirations, and to the needs of diverse firms across industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The public sector will bring forward our hiring to meet long-term needs, like early childhood education, healthcare and long-term care.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many businesses have stepped forward, with openings in a wide range of job roles, such as computer engineers and machine operators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage more businesses to do even more in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To equip our people to take on these jobs, we will expand capacity in Career Conversion Programmes, such as in Place-and-Train conversion programmes under the Adapt and Grow Initiative, and Company-Led Training programmes under the TechSkills Accelerator or TeSA initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: TeSA has been successful since its launch in Budget 2016.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As of December 2019, over a thousand have been trained in partnership with industry leaders such as Accenture, DBS Bank and Google.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over 90% of them have been emplaced in ICT-related roles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I look forward to more industry partners coming on board, to help prepare more Singaporeans for a future where digitalisation becomes increasingly important.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second component in this SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package is traineeships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide jobseekers with a wider range of traineeships to gain industry-relevant experience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Trainees may be emplaced in jobs with their host companies at the end of their traineeships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even if they do not, they would have learnt valuable skills for other jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In total, we target to create about 25,000 traineeship positions this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Resilience Budget, I announced the SGUnited Traineeships programme targeted at our local first-time jobseekers, where WSG funds the training allowances with host companies, for up to 12 months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad to see strong interest from more than a thousand host companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The public sector is also keen to offer new traineeship opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this momentum, I will more than double the provision, to provide 21,000 traineeships this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our technology and innovation drive, these traineeships will include technology-related areas that are in high demand or emerging rapidly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: DSTA will offer diploma holders the opportunity to build skills in fast-growing technology areas like IT and engineering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Agencies in our research and development sector, including our Universities, A*STAR research institutes, AI Singapore and SGInnovate will work with local deep-tech companies and start-ups for trainees to work with industry partners on real-world science and technology projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will include areas such as software learning and AI.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As earlier announced by the Minister for Manpower, these traineeships will be progressively offered from 1 June this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will pay special attention to mid-career jobseekers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We understand that many are worried about their job prospects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, we will create a new SGUnited Mid-Career Traineeships scheme for unemployed mid-career jobseekers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our agencies will work with interested companies to provide 4,000 traineeships for our mid-career jobseekers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This scheme specifically caters to the needs of mid-career individuals, to learn new skills and embark on new careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Also, included under the Traineeships category are WSG's Attach-and-Train programmes under the Adapt and Grow Initiative targeted at mid-career individuals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also scale these up, to provide meaningful traineeship opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jobseekers can upgrade their skills while looking for a job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Participants in this SGUnited Skills programme will take industry-relevant and certifiable training courses full-time at highly subsidised rates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The course fees can be substantially, if not fully offset by their SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The courses will be delivered by companies and Continuing Education Training (CET) Centres, including Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jobseekers will be given opportunities to apply their training through attachments or participation in company projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help them focus on their training and job search.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This programme will be rolled out progressively from July 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fourth component is a horizontal layer of our SGUnited Jobs and Skills package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, our traineeships and skills training are to help our people to secure jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In these uncertain times, I understand why many employers, even if they are doing well, are reluctant to hire.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support employers in hiring, I will provide a hiring incentive to employers to hire local workers who have gone through eligible traineeship and training schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Unity Budget, I announced a hiring incentive under the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with other support, such as the special SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 to every Singaporean aged 40 to 60 in 2020, we are providing specially enhanced support for jobs and training for this group.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If needed, they can also benefit from other support schemes this period, such as the COVID-19 Support Grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Further, I will also expand the hiring incentive to cover workers of all ages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am greatly encouraged by how our tripartite partners are working together, going all out to provide strong support to our skills and jobs initiatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Business Federation is currently the programme manager for SGUnited Traineeships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are working hard to bring as many host companies on board and as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NTUC, besides supporting current workers, is reaching out to fresh graduates through the Young NTUC Movement to consider the SGUnited Traineeships programme as an option after graduation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some employers have stepped forward to offer jobs and traineeships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This not only contributes to the national effort but it is also a far-sighted move to build longer term capabilities for their companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage employers to also make good use of the strong support we provide to upskill your existing workers during this downtime so that they can emerge stronger when business picks up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members will appreciate the range of schemes in the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ensure that the strategy can be implemented well and to sustain the momentum of current efforts, careful design of the schemes and attention to implementation details are critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam, as Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and former Finance as well as Education Minister, has both detailed knowledge and deep expertise in this issue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have requested him to chair a National Jobs Council to oversee this very important work and I thank him for agreeing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Jobs Council will be focused on creating jobs and building deep skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This important effort will be integrated with the work of the Future Economy Council on the overall upgrading of our economy through the Industry Transformation Maps in each cluster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will also be integrated into our Emerging Stronger Task Force work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, we can marshal all our experiences and expertise to manage the huge changes that are coming our way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Jobs Council will provide details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about what we will do to protect livelihoods, create new opportunities and help our workers access good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will now turn to how we will protect our families and the community and to help Singaporeans cope with this period of uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the last three Budgets, we provided direct support to all Singaporeans and provided more for the lower income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the month of April, the Temporary Relief Fund assisted 450,000 individuals who were in need of immediate financial help before other support schemes came on stream.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many have written to my colleagues and me to express their appreciation for the help received.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are very glad that you have found this helpful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to provide help for immediate needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 Support Grant is now in place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It covers those who have lost their jobs, are placed on no-pay leave or will see salaries significantly reduced in the coming months due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the three weeks after the COVID-19 Support Grant started, we received about 48,000 applications.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are committed to providing help to those who have been badly affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For self-employed persons, we are providing direct cash assistance through the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, or SIRS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Self-employed persons who do not automatically qualify or have marginally missed the criteria can approach NTUC.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So far, NTUC has received over 60,000 applications and is working hard to process them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Applicants can expect to hear from NTUC within a month of submitting their application.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also encourage all self-employed persons to make full use of the SEP Training Support Scheme to train and upskill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some self-employed persons are re-assessing their career options, looking at industries which are hiring.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will support you to access training programmes to make the transition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help all Singaporeans with their household expenses during this period of uncertainty, I introduced a comprehensive Care and Support Package in my previous Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Adult Singaporeans would have received their Solidarity Payment of $600 in cash.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am encouraged to hear that some have donated the payout to help others with greater needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Care and Support Package has other components that will flow in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, lower- and middle-income Singaporeans will be receiving their remaining Care and Support – Cash payout of $300 or $600 in June.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Parents with young Singaporean children will also receive the $300 cash payout at the same time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are on top of permanent support schemes such as the GST Voucher-Cash, which will be paid out in August.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Earlier, I announced in the Unity Budget that I would double the amount of U-Save rebates through a one-off GST Voucher – U-Save Special Payment for eligible HDB households to help with utility bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Larger households with five or more members get more and can receive up to $1,000 in U-Save rebates this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans have given us the feedback that while they are saving on transport fares and other charges, they are expecting to spend more on their utility bills as they stay home during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will cover all property types and will be credited in the July or August utilities bill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Altogether, we have put in place numerous schemes to tide our households through this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Members can see, we have payments that will be coming on stream, particularly, every month – some form of payment to our households to support our households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During the stay-home period, families are making fuller use of digital technology for home-based learning, entertainment, ordering meals and keeping in touch with families and friends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The value of access to digital technology is clear.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During COVID-19, being able to connect with each other safely has enabled support, especially for vulnerable members of our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In a post-COVID-19 world, having all on board digital channels will open up exciting new possibilities for different members of the community to engage with and support each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, digital inclusion should be an important way for us to strengthen social resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Regardless of age or resources, all members of our society should have access to digital resources with no one left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To this end, we will provide help for specific groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first group is our students who have gone through about four weeks of home-based learning during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Education will announce details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Seniors, who are more vulnerable if infected, are staying home during this period and many will have to continue doing so to protect themselves from COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Silver Generation Office has been keeping in touch with seniors with care needs and weaker family support through telephone calls and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enable seniors to stay in contact with their families and friends and for our care teams and volunteers to reach out more effectively, IMDA will launch a Seniors Go Digital movement to support seniors to adopt digital channels and equip them with the digital skills to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will require all-round support from family, friends and the wider community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will launch a Digital Ambassadors movement to rally the community and volunteers to support our seniors to acquire digital skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For seniors from lower income households who wish to learn but are unable to afford devices, we will provide them with financial support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly encourage our youths who have the digital skills, as well as corporates, to step forward to reach out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Communications and Information and IMDA will share more details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides digital inclusion, another pillar for social resilience is our social service agencies and charities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are key partners who have been supporting families and vulnerable groups during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the years ahead, a stronger social service sector will be even more critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last Saturday, Ministers Grace Fu, Indranee and Desmond joined me in a video conference with leaders of our social service agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They shared with us how they have been using digital means to reach out to the diverse clients they are serving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has not been easy, but they tried and found it useful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are very encouraged by their can-do spirit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many found, in their words, "opportunities in adversity", and were able to "turn the challenges during the circuit breaker into new areas of strength".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While these cannot replace the human touch, they found digital tools, a useful complement that would help them better reach out to their clients even after the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To serve their clients better, several social service agencies have started on the digitalisation journey and many want to press ahead with their transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Project Belanja! by Food from the Heart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beneficiaries can simply scan a QR code at partner food stalls to obtain a hot meal, instead of having volunteers go door-to-door to deliver food.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This creative idea supports our hawkers and allows beneficiaries to get freshly cooked food, while our social service agencies save costs and reduce food wastage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support the building of digital capabilities as a key priority, the National Council of Social Service, or NCSS, is mobilising corporate partners to lend their expertise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many have stepped up, including ThunderQuote which developed self-help guides on remote working tools and TechLadies which provides general consultancy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MSF and NCSS will continue to support the social service sector in building capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Funding is currently available through the VWO-Charities Capability Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In future, these initiatives can also be funded by the Community Capability Trust, which I announced at the Unity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While continuing to be passionate about supporting the vulnerable in our community, our charities and social service agencies are facing difficulties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The leaders appreciate the support from the Jobs Support Scheme, but they are facing falling donations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes donations raised through approved digital platforms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly urge Singaporeans and residents in Singapore who are able, to donate generously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NCSS had earlier set up the Invictus Fund to provide additional support to social service agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Fund will support our social service agencies to maintain service continuity, retain staff and adopt technology to transform their work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge our social service agencies to accelerate their digitalisation efforts, scale up capabilities and share resources and efforts to solve common challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to provide our strongest support for you so that you can serve your clients better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, we are dedicating close to $100 billion or $92.9 billion to be precise, about 20% of our GDP, to support our people in this battle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the largest Overall Budget deficit in Singapore's history since our independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Fortitude Budget will be funded out of Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the second draw on Past Reserves this financial year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Past Reserves are our strategic asset, built up through the prudence and hard work of our people, across generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has always upheld the principle that our Past Reserves are to be used only in exceptional circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, we used up almost all our accumulated surpluses since the start of this term of Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But what we need to deal effectively with COVID-19 has grown so much that we have no choice but to draw on Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our fight against COVID-19, our Past Reserves have been critical in enabling us to respond comprehensively and robustly to the situation at hand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have to deploy it in a deliberate manner, and at decisive moments, in this battle against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the earlier Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, the President gave approval to draw up to $21 billion from our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This allowed us to safeguard jobs, keep the economy going, and provide direct assistance to Singaporeans during this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also told Members then, that I was prepared to propose to the President to make further draws on Past Reserves, should it be necessary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, the impact of COVID-19 on Singapore has deepened.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lives and livelihoods are at stake, and we are moving to secure our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After a challenging circuit breaker period, we are now preparing to re-open our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To do so in a safe and calibrated manner and to continue to support our people, we are proposing a further draw on our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Prime Minister met with the President to share the Government's considerations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministers Gan Kim Yong, Lawrence Wong, Chan Chun Sing, and Indranee Rajah joined me last week, to brief the President and the Council of Presidential Advisers (CPA) on the Government's assessment of the situation, the details of the measures and the resources needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As President Halimah stated in a Facebook post yesterday and I quote, "Indeed, this crisis is unprecedented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a very significant amount, necessitated by the very exceptional nature of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members of this House know how strict I have been on prudence and my Ministry's emphasis on value-for-money spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Public Accounts Committee has also been scrutinising the Government's expenditure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have deliberated long and hard on the measures and went through many rounds of deliberations with fellow Ministers and my staff.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have also discussed with the Prime Minister and my Cabinet colleagues before finalising this set of measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been an unprecedented crisis that is still changing rapidly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I am grateful that we have the fiscal resources to mount this response and the unity, resilience and solidarity of our people to battle this together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have a responsibility to make the best use of these resources, to keep our people safe, to save jobs and transform businesses and to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every dollar that we have saved has been saved by careful counting over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In spending this national savings now, we must make every dollar spent count.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we have the resources and the will to do what is needed in fighting COVID-19, we must continue to stay nimble and adaptive in this rapidly evolving situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are dealing, as many have said, with a very smart and agile virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To cater for urgent and unforeseen expenditure needs which have yet to be provided for under the Supply Act, the Constitution provides for Parliament to create Contingencies Funds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each year, in our annual Budget, we set aside a total of $3 billion as a buffer in the Contingencies Fund and the Development Contingencies Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With COVID-19, we are facing unprecedented levels of uncertainty – it is uncertain how the pandemic will evolve, if there will be a second or even third wave, and if, and when, vaccines will be available.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The uncertainty on the medical front is fuelling the uncertainty in the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members will appreciate that within less than four months, we are deploying four Budgets to protect Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
