text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew said this during the post SARS period, in his experience "in any battle, the morale and the spirit of the people will decide the outcome.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew knew at that time it was going to be tough, like climbing up the face of a cliff.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But we, like he said, "must have the guts and determination to climb the face of the cliff and we will climb up the face of the cliff!" And if I might add, with fortitude and not just the hindsight vision of 20-20.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The relief for sectors hit hardest and businesses still unable to open is very much welcomed.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It has been months of hard work by the Government.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Many businesses are affected during this period, with many unsure of their future.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This COVID-19 pandemic is causing unparalleled uncertainty across many fronts.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One industry that I am immersed in is the sports and fitness industry.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: With the reliefs, businesses may have less worries for the next month or so but with the uncertainty of when they can resume operations due to safe distancing measures, or when Singaporeans will come back to sports due to their own personal concerns of safety, it is difficult for them to plan for the future.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Most sports and fitness activities stopped even before the circuit breaker started as there were already other measures in place to flatten the curve at that point of time.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Most gyms and studios have frozen or adjusted their memberships to retain clients, while some are conducting online classes.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Planned events from competitions to fundraising events have been cancelled.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: All these had led to significant revenue loss across the sector.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These are businesses that keep our society healthy and resilient and the COVID-19 pandemic is putting them at a risk.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports and fitness helps to build a stronger national identity.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It improves our health, productivity, reduces medical expenses and enhances social cohesion.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports and fitness are for people of all ages, abilities and walks of life.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, the Sports and Fitness industry is one of the industries that has a huge knock-on effect to the rest of the economy since the Sports and Fitness industry is not just about people exercising or playing games – it also involves many other sectors and businesses such as tourism, retail, events management, marketing, sports education and training, support services such as Public Relations, fundraising and so on.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that we must now proceed with caution as we slowly emerge after two months of circuit breaker measures and I wholeheartedly agree with it.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We do not want our efforts to go to waste.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, there will be many safe distancing measures in placed.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: For example, only being able to have one person per swimming lane or the spacing between each individual has to be huge, hence, only accommodating six people in the studio at all times.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This cut in numbers will result in a low income coming in.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The Sports and Fitness industry is finding it difficult to survive.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Now, as they already had to dig in the reserves for the past two months or so.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Besides paying their employees who may have already taken a pay cut, there are also other expenses.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If unable to cope, these schools and clubs might start closing down and it will affect our pipeline as the schools and clubs are an important pathway for our sporting performance.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Right now, what will be helpful is if we have a clearer view.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports and Fitness is a highly varied industry, with many different kinds of activities – from outdoor sports, to personal training sessions, to tennis where players stand on opposing ends of the court, to swimming, to indoor activities such as yoga and kickboxing.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: There are questions that many businesses are asking – when the numbers remain low, what will the plan be?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: What about indoor facilities and when these facilities can start again, what will the most number of people be allowed in at any point in time?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These details will help this industry be more certain and help the industry chart the path ahead.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: With all the positives that this industry brings to Singaporeans, we still want to see them around after the COVID-19 pandemic so that they can continue contributing positively to the community.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If we continue doing our parts to keep each other safe, we can look forward to getting back into sporting activities safely.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The rest of the services associated with the Sports and Fitness industry that I had highlighted above would also be able to better plan their respective businesses and know how to react to the new norms when the time comes.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We will all have to adapt to a new kind of normal, to include safe distancing measures and ensure we come out of this stronger.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We talk about digitising in times like this.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, the Sports and Fitness industry is one of the sectors that is harder to digitise, as its very essence is to get people to go out and be active, healthy and interact socially.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, payments can be done online, some activities can shift online but It will be hard to do things like instructions online especially for our younger, older and special population groups that require a greater level of supervision.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Certain activities that require a physical medium like swimming, will also lose out, because, say for example, why would parents want their children to do land activities online for swimming classes when they can take up a land sport instead?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, this is also a great opportunity for the Government to take a more holistic approach in improving the entire industry and provide the infrastructural approach and guidance to help the industry grow.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This could be done by taking a more inclusive approach in education and towards the sporting enterprises, to help them grow together with this economy.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports is nowhere near the top of our priority list, but what we learn from sports will also play a big part in our education.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Institutions should embrace sporting values into their own culture.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When we adequately and holistically impart the fun and advantages of sport in them at a young age, it helps to translate into lifelong participation in sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Personally, being actively involved in sports since a young age has helped me greatly.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It has not only helped me physically but also mentally and emotionally.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When I was younger, I was not a very good student.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I did not get good grades, but after winning a gold medal at the Paralympics in Beijing, I came back and did my "O" levels.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I did not hit my expectations but thankfully I managed to get into Polytechnic.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Then, I thought to myself, why not use the perseverance, grit, focus and everything I learnt from swimming to apply to my studies?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I was then laser focused on getting my grades up and started to do pretty well and eventually got into SMU.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If not for swimming, I would not be where i am today.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When kids start participating more in sports, their families watch them play and that helps with family bonding.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This leads to a more supportive family and community.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Parents are our first sport coaches and they impart social and family values through play.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, as we age, other important values can be imparted through sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: For our sporting culture to grow, the Sports and Fitness industry must grow too.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sport Singapore has done a commendable job with Active SG, Singapore Sports Institute, Sports Cares and more.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We have amazing facilities and host world class events.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We must continue our efforts and continue to improve by growing the sports industry.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As a regulator, an approach would be to work closer with the private sector to enhance capabilities, resources and business opportunities.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Sports and fitness businesses are an important pillar of this industry as they bring expertise, knowledge and organised play to the table.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: They employ passionate Singaporeans that are constantly shaping the lives of people of all ages and backgrounds.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: And we need them to thrive so as to achieve the outcomes I spoke about earlier.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly, to build sustainability, we also need to accelerate the growth of businesses who have great potential.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Another approach is to take a more inclusionary path in organising the Sports and Fitness industry.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: SportSG as a regulator has done a fantastic job with its various initiatives to get people to participate in sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, the impact may be greater and faster, if we allow the Sports and Fitness industry operators to help in this process.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One of the ways we could do this is to allow the Sports and Fitness industry to fill in the gaps and allow them to grow, rather than to take a one size fits all approach.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In the long run, we will have a more vibrant, sustainable sporting Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In this period of time, how many Singaporeans have thought about how somebody who is blind and living alone while observing safe distancing measures is coping?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If a student with muscular dystrophy needs an oxygen tank with a breathing mask and their teacher asks them to put on a face mask or shield, which would mean that they have to take the oxygen tank off, so that the teacher does not get into trouble for not observing the measures.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: How would this affect the student and their family?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In times like this, it is especially crucial to look out for those who may be struggling more than others.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I recognise that SGEnable and Social Service Agency partners are helping people with special needs and the vulnerable in the community.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I see the C.A.R.E initiative by Mediacorp Enable Fund aiming to help people with disabilities and their care-givers ride out the COVID-19 pandemic as the impact on this community has been, in their words "disproportionately huge".

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This fund is driven by public donations and we greatly appreciate that.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Together, we can all continue playing a part to ensure no one falls through the cracks.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The lack of information to certain disability groups in Singapore is counter-productive to the effort in combating the COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The right to information is crucial for ensuring public awareness, trust and fighting misinformation.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We have to ensure that public health information and communication is accessible on all important media publications.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It would be ideal if a Singapore Sign Language interpreter is present for all live, recorded events and communications.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This includes national addresses, press briefings and live social media.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Over the weekend, I was watching a live panel discussion on social media – Get Active TV that featured Minister Fu and SportSG.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: They too had a Singapore Sign Language interpreter and live notes.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I am very heartened at this great development and hopefully this can continue on all other updates and media during this time and beyond.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We look forward to a time when all media comes with live Singapore Sign Language interpretation.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The images we put out out there have to be inclusive and enable the independence of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs).

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: For example, the current level of safe entry QR code tends to be placed a bit too high.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: A consideration could be to place it at varying easy to reach heights as we have done so with many lift buttons.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Next, supermarkets have done a great job at dealing with the increased demand and restocking of shelves.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Many PWDs are finding it hard to get deliveries.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This may be a combination of there not being enough slots as well as the accessibility of websites not being optimal.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Other than food, access to medical prescriptions and other health care supplies are highly essential as well.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Existing volunteer networks can be activated to help deliver these supplies.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If possible, doctors should be able to see their at-risk patients online for check ups because they are afraid of going to hospitals to get exposed yet they do need to see the doctor for their regular check up.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Besides medications, some disabilities require more home care and physiotherapy services.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: These services cannot be stopped as it will bring detrimental results mentally and physically to PWDs and their family.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In some cases, not getting their physiotherapy will result in irreversible loss of muscle or contracture which will permanently impact their quality of life.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In just two weeks' time, they would have permanently lost quite a bit of function.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Employment of persons with disabilities remains relatively low in Singapore and for those that are employed, not all are fortunate enough to be able to execute their work from home.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The main issues for PWDs working from home are whether their employers can adequately physically and financially provide the assistive devices and technology they may need to work at home.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Many themselves are not able to do so because of their socio-economic challenges.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: For PWDs whose job scope used to be done predominantly face-to-face, the added need for technology to be able to potentially do the work online would mean increased spending.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Schemes such as NEU PC to provide laptops to students from low-income families are welcome.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: However, assistive technology and aids are usually more expensive to purchase.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This translates to a loss of income and opportunities to retrain or learn new skills.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Socially, the lack of access to IT equipment can mean missing out on opportunities to maintain or grow connections with friends and families.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This can in turn negatively impact those with psycho-social disabilities, increasing mental stress and straining existing coping mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As we are encouraged to work from home or have home-based learning, what assistance is being provided to ensure that the assistive technology is available in all homes for persons with disabilities?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Many of them face socio-economic challenges and may not be able to afford IT equipment, assistive aids and broadband to help them better cope with life in this period of time.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Persons with disabilities who had jobs that cannot be done online or had difficulties finding employment before the COVID-19 pandemic are even more concerned that they will not be able to return to work or get a job.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: They are also concerned about the accessibility or inclusivity of job training and retraining programmes.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The financial assistance provided by the Temporary Relief fund, COVID-19 Support Grant and other schemes such as SIRS are greatly appreciated.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Those with disabilities already often have higher healthcare and personal care costs and these costs are likely to increase as alternative or emergency arrangements are made during the circuit breaker or the phases after that.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: We need a fast response as a delay might cause harm to some individuals in special situations.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: This touch point ensures that there is two-way communication about the COVID-19 response and we can identify the gaps quickly and share best practices.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The best way to find out what people need is to ask them.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In this pandemic, we have to look out for all so that we can truly be an inclusive and united Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We then called on Singaporeans that we have to use masks appropriately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Please do not hoard so that we will have enough supplies, especially for those groups that need them most.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When there is new information, there is new evidence, we would likewise adopt an open and transparent manner in our communications because we know that is important in our collective fight against this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In that vein, can I ask the Senior Minister of State, with regard to the decision earlier this week to stop usage of face shields except for certain classes of individuals, how was that decision originally taken to allow for face shields and then, a u-turn made thereafter to limit it to specific classes?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: How did that information change from the health experts I imagine that the Government has access to?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is as Mr Singh himself alluded to – based on the advice from medical professionals.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I ask what were the reasons given by those experts for that change?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I think the MTF and the medical professionals have provided the explanation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is about protecting everybody's health and safety.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As we move into Phase One of our opening, we will see increased interaction within the community, among people.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And therefore, we will have to make sure that additional safeguards are put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, we allowed face shields to be used.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we still allow face shields to be used in specific situations where mask-wearing is not practical.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One example which we gave was during teaching.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Teachers need to make sure that their teaching is clearly heard and it is important for them to see and to interact with the children.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is really my key point – that we have publicly explained that and these are all in the public domain.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While there has been a comprehensive range of schemes and measures rolled out, I would like to focus on a few key areas in my speech.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has seen the Government take bold, unprecedented steps to help our businesses stay afloat.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As most of us know, two of the biggest overheads that businesses must manage are manpower costs and rent.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To help companies manage rental cost, the Government first introduced several measures such as rebate on property tax and waiver of rental for tenants of Government properties.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But this is not a common crisis and this uncommon step of intervening demonstrates the commitment of the Government to help SMEs weather through the storm.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am in firm support of this and while this is a positive boost for SME tenants, there is also the possibility that a significant number of smaller landlords could themselves be small companies or even individual owners who are dependent on this rental income to meet their income needs and financial commitments.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Waiving the rental income for their tenants might thus result in them being deprived of revenue or even being slapped with penalties from financial institutions because they are unable to service their loans.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What help and support would the Government be able to provide smaller landlords in such situations?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And if these smaller landlords are unable to fulfill their financial obligations, would the Government be able to intervene to mandate that financial institutions perhaps could suspend loan repayments until this group of landlords are able to start collecting their rental income?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Despite all the measures that we have put in place to support companies through COVID-19, not all companies will survive the downturn and the global economic slowdown.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is heartening to know that one of the major thrusts of the main and supplementary Budgets is to preserve jobs and a new National Jobs Council will be set up to look at job creation and the deep skilling of workers.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: COVID-19 has transformed the way we think about work.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In many countries, what was traditionally known as "3D jobs" – dirty, dangerous and demeaning – are now considered as important services that keep countries going, that keep communities going.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Frontline jobs that were not given much attention in the past are now being recognised as being operationally essential.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: COVID-19, indeed, has created some jobs that were unheard of prior to the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In January this year, we would have no clue what a Safe Distancing Ambassador, a test swabber, a swab assistant or a temperature taker was.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But they have now entered the lexicon of our everyday use – in terms of the language that we use.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, as reported in the media this week, we will soon have Digital Ambassadors to help hawkers and senior citizens to learn digital skills.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These jobs were clearly created out of the need to manage the challenges of COVID-19 and also help provide part-time employment to those who were made redundant by the crisis.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the mid term, certain jobs like Safe Distancing Ambassadors will continue to be relevant but in the long run, some of these jobs could be less necessary as we internalise the need to practise safe distancing, when a vaccine for COVID-19 becomes available or as we level up on the digital front.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To ensure that this precious workforce does not become redundant when these semi-permanent positions are no longer required, how can we future-proof the career paths of currently employed Singaporeans and to help our people retrain, up-skill and continue to pivot and shapeshift, as it were, to stay relevant as we respond to the new normal.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I sincerely hope that this is something that the National Jobs Council will need to consider as it balances short-term national needs with the long-term prospects for our people.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The next topic, Mr Speaker, Sir, is on digitalisation and education.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the early days of COVID-19, there was a meme circulating that the virus was more effective than CEOs and CTOs in pushing for digital transformation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This meme turned out to be quite prophetic and in the past few months, we have seen companies accelerating digital implementation and making remote work platforms mainstream in somewhat record time.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The same could be said about our schools.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the one hand, this figure is encouraging as it shows that our children have adapted well to learning on digital channels.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet, on the other hand, it was reported that MOE had to loan out thousands of computing devices and internet dongles to families.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am strongly advocating for the latter, Mr Speaker.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition to have the opportunity for Singapore businesses to benefit from both hardware production and software development, the benefits to our children will be myriad.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With more control over the design and functionality of this device, this all-in-one custom-designed learning device could function as a lap-top, a tablet, an e-text book, and a communication tool.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A veritable digital "Swiss-Army Education Knife" of sorts.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The ownership of this multi-function device might also eliminate the need for piles of back-breaking, physical textbooks year after year after year.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Going to school in the future could be as easy as just bringing along this device and all forms of learning and work submission can be done digitally on a unified platform.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Quite literally, we are putting the world in the hands of our school children.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The software could be customised and adapted to suit the pace of learning for different children while also providing personal insights to how each student engages and interacts along the learning journey.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The operating system of this device could function like an enhanced version of the MOE's present Student Learning System (SLS) and would allow for more coordinated and unified communication and work planning.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: No school-going child should be deprived of their own personal learning device.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would give our children, especially those from lower income background, a sense of pride and ownership that they have their own personal device that will allow them to navigate the same digital and virtual education landscapes as their peers.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore could very well be the first nation in the world to achieve our vision of "smart learning." Mr Speaker, Sir, 2020 will no doubt go down in memory as one of the most volatile years the world, and Singapore, has experienced.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Yet in every crisis, lie opportunities to innovate and transform and the past 100 days have certainly seen our companies and schools doing just that, as they have experimented and innovated with new methods of doing business and conducting lessons.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And we can be masters of our own destiny and forge our own uniquely Singaporean path through this crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Post-circuit breaker, contractors are anxious to resume work quickly.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many have paid for material or are leasing equipment which are now sitting idle and since contractors are typically paid based on progress payments, no work means no payment; and we understand then anxiety.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While we want to resume construction activity quickly, it is equally important that we do so safely.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we do not want to restart hastily as a new case could easily cause another outbreak or new cluster among construction workers either on a construction site or in the dormitories.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such a resurgence of infection would not only endanger the health of our workers and the wider community, but also bring the construction industry to a halt to get.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is in our common interest for construction work to resume in a phased and controlled manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond this list of projects if firms have cleared workers and have put in place necessary safe management measures, firms can submit their applications to BCA and once approved they will be able to resume their projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On the Government end, my colleagues have been working hard on multiple fronts to allow construction activities to resume faster.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the inter-agency Task Force has been systematically and progressively clearing workers living in dormitories to ensure they are well so that they can return to work.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many contractors have shared with us their frustration about not knowing what is going on in the dormitories, as workers have been moved around several times during these few months.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They would also like to know in advance when their workers can be tested and cleared for work so they can make plans for the projects to resume.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They have asked for more information and updates on the dormitories' clearance situation.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members would recognise the scale and complexity of the Task Force operations as there are 43 purpose-built dormitories and more than a 1,000 factory converted dormitories and construction temporary quarters housing more than 300,000 workers and the outbreak situation each dormitory is different.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will provide more regular updates to our industry, including a rolling forecast of the dormitory clearance schedule to help employers and their clients plan ahead.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For workers living in the community, we have also set aside testing capacity to test construction workers regularly to ensure the health and safety and that of the wider community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has shared concerns of contractors with the latest MOM announcement on foreign worker levy rebates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Government's intention was to enable workers to be temporarily seconded to other firms to optimise manpower distribution, so that more projects can restart sooner.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, some of them may require their workers for their own projects that are about to start and cannot second their workers to other projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MOM and BCA will review this and we will work with them and the industry to find better ways to achieve this optimisation for the benefit of the entire sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Er Dr Lee asked about the new requirements for existing factory converted dormitories and construction temporary quarters.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have piloted the new space norms for new quick build dormitories that will be put up by the end of the year and we have been working with industry associations to make sure these requirements are practical, even as we seek to achieve safety and will be prepared to consider further inputs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So far, we have approved more than 20 requests from contractors who wish to build new CTQs or FCDs for their workers and will continue to facilitate such requests where possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have received feedback that the COVID-19 restart criteria for construction are stringent.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There is a project with a single owner on a single site with all workers staying on site.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The workers have not left the site since end March, even before circuit breaker.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Full attention was given to protection and safety by all levels of management, such as ensuring proper segregation among workers, including not allowing workers from different levels of the dormitories to mix.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Yet that project had an infection prevalence rate of close to 30% amongst its workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I share this example which was shared with me to show how infectious disease is and how difficult it can be to prevent spreading from a single case to affecting many more who live and work together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, imagine how much more challenging in might be for projects with workers living in different accommodation or having to move between different sites, as is the case with many projects with main contractors and several layers of sub-contractors and specialist contractors.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we understand the concerns of companies and will work closely with the industry associations at firms to look at the requirements to ensure that they are practically implementable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also providing training to help companies put in place safe management measures by offering a course for safe management offices or SMOs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the month of June alone, BCA and SCAL will train close to 20,000 such officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: BCA will give priority to train SMOs for projects that are ready to start first.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: BCA is also ramping up capacity further through tech-enabled learning modules.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We know there is a lot of information that is being put out about COVID-19 related measures, sometimes from multiple Ministries and agencies, day after day.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Given how fluid and dynamic the situation is, contractors have told us that they are sometimes confused, lost, overwhelmed.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, if companies have questions or concerns, whether about testing their workers or constructing new temporary quarters, they need to only approach BCA who will coordinate with other relevant agencies to make the necessary arrangements or seek the necessary approvals.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Because of the current situation, BCA has received a huge surge of calls, emails and queries, and we are ramping up our capabilities to better support our sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We understand that firms are very concerned about their finances during this period when the projects have yet to restart.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Government has also announced rental offsets for qualifying SME tenants.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Even after construction projects restart, we recognise that firms have to bear additional costs to meet the new COVID requirements, which were not priced into the existing contracts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And in the long term, the Government will continue to support the construction industry and provide assistance to cope with the additional costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will share more details on the specific measures when we are ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise the importance of the construction industry because without them, we would not have our homes, our schools, our hospitals and other services.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we will do what we can to help as many companies as possible tide through this crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And that is also why we have been working closely with our industry partners, such as a Singapore Contractors Association Limited (SCAL), the Specialists Trade Alliance of Singapore or STARS, and the Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore or REDAS, to address the many issues that the industry is facing during this period.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, Minister of State Zaqy and I held a video conference meeting with them just two days ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This was our third meeting in three weeks and we will continue to do so regularly.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, SCAL had earlier provided feedback that there are some construction S Pass and work permit holders who do not live in dormitories, work only in offices and do not visit work sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In consultation with MOH, we agreed to remove the regular testing requirement for this group of employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was also feedback that a company had to approach several different agencies to obtain the necessary approval to build new temporary living quarters or to convert existing workplaces and factories into living quarters.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Participants told us at these discussions which involve a number of Government agencies being brought together are useful and we will continue to coordinate closely and keep our lines of engagement with industry open.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira spoke yesterday about our dependence on foreign workers, including in the construction sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our efforts to raise productivity in the construction industry has been ongoing for decades.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In line with the construction industry transformation map under the work of the Future Economic Council or FEC, we have indeed been working with industry to reduce our reliance on foreign workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But this will require major structural changes to the industry and to how construction work is done.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been pushing for greater adoption of technology, such as through design for manufacturing and assembly, building information modelling and digitisation of the sector from end to end.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will, in turn, create higher skilled jobs, including many good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, with design for manufacturing and assembly or DFMA, we will need more production managers, quality assurance personnel and logistics and supply chain planners and automated production facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Even our foreign workers that take on such jobs will need to be higher skilled.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, the construction sector will not be able to reduce our foreign worker reliance to zero as there will still be many lower skilled jobs in the sector that Singaporeans do not want to take up.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We appreciate the contribution of our foreign guest workers who have come here to Singapore to make an honest living for themselves and their families and it is incumbent on us to also take care of them when they are unwell.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On one hand, I am relieved that the circuit breaker has officially ended.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On the other hand, with no immediate end in sight to the COVID-19 battle, I am worried about what the next few months, rather years, have in store for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I speak for my generation and those young at heart when I say that there are many questions running through our minds.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Have we faced a situation like this before?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Do we have what it takes to get through this and emerge stronger?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: From a forced Independence to the communist threat to the racial riots to recessions to multiple global financial crises to even pandemics, we have come through it all.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And it was those defining moments that have always brought the best out of our people.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As we deal with the immediate issues and pressing problems facing us, I remind myself, Members of this house and my fellow Singaporeans that COVID-19 is offering us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to make seismic shifts in the way we have been doing things.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This shall form the crux of my speech today.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I begin by speaking on the theme of our responsibility to the nation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition to COVID-19, we continue to face long-term pressures such as the geopolitical tensions between America and China, stagnating growth and more nationalist and protectionist tendencies around the world.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Given that our reserves form the basis of our NIRC revenue, what is the projected revenue impact of this large drawdown?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And a mere two years later, the amount drawn was returned back to the reserves in 2011.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We owe it to our future generations to safeguard their future as our forefathers have done so for us.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: My third question thus echoes the concerns which I heard in this Chamber yesterday.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Consequently, we cannot afford to be complacent in how the money is being spent.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Even as Deputy Prime Minister has assured us that the Public Accounts Committee has been scrutinising Government's expenditure, we need to instill a mindset of "active audit" to ensure that funds channeled for the various schemes and projects are indeed being spent wisely.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This crisis is an opportunity for us to re-imagine work.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: At various times, this House has debated the importance of improving our work-life balance and having a more sustainable way of life.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our experience over the last three months has shown that being present in the office and having face-to-face meetings is not absolutely necessary for many of us.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Members of this House and fellow Singaporeans will be surprised to know that the SGUnited Buka Puasa initiative involving multiple Government agencies, private companies and community organisations was conceptualised, planned and operationalised virtually, without even a single physical meeting.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And I am sure there are many other such projects.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We have, within a very short period of time, adapted to working through video conferencing, private messaging, emails and even the good old fashion phone calls.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: To quote the CEO of a leading software firm, COVID-19 has resulted in two years of digital transformation in just two months.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We need to build upon this rather than going back to old ways.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: It is time that we reconsider a new model for our companies.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to offer some solutions and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Established companies like Microsoft have demonstrated that a four-day work week can increase productivity by up to 40%.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Twitter's CEO recently announced that it will allow its employees to work from home "forever".

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In New Zealand, a four-day work week to promote better work life balance and domestic tourism as a means to help the economy is being considered.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As the Government prepares for Phase Two, we should re-evaluate our traditional model of work.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Second, I hope that after COVID-19, telecommuting will not disappear but will be a more permanent feature.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As the Government prepares to work with our companies to begin the job creation process, it is incumbent on us to incentivise the creation of jobs which will allow telecommuting.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, we will no longer exclude those who may be unable to work in a traditional nine-to-five environment for various reasons.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: President Halimah recently said, and I quote, "Imagine how many more women with young children could remain in the workforce if they could telecommute.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Imagine the kind of skills and talents among women that we could retain to benefit our society and economy.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: With dual income families more of a necessity today, we should make it easier for women with family obligations to work." Mr Speaker, it is not just women with care-giving duties who will benefit from this arrangement but many more.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, I came across a very moving commentary by Mr Jonathan Tiong, a fourth year student from NUS.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: He is a disabled person who will soon be entering the workforce.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Being a wheelchair user, one of the biggest obstacles he faced was travel, which he defined as the mere act of leaving his home.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Unlike an able-bodied person, he cannot just get up and go wherever he wants.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The logistics of transport invariably involves at least one other person for him.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: He shared from his personal experience that video conferencing will help disabled persons and people with disabilities to integrate better into society by allowing them to lead more active professional and social lives.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In creating openings and retaining these segments of the population in the workforce, we can then create a workforce that is not only fair to all but also ensure that we maximise our potential to the fullest.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I am confident that the National Jobs Council helmed by Senior Minister Tharman will also look into this matter.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On digital transformation and innovation, since 2014, the Smart Nation initiative has been quietly transforming and enriching the lives of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: At the World Economic Forum in Davos in 2019, Deputy Prime Minister stated that Singapore needs to work towards repositioning itself to becoming a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As we restart our economy, the importance of the Smart Nation initiative and the words of Deputy Prime Minister cannot be more true.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: To ride the new wave, we need our people to be digitally enabled in every sense of the word.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: What this means is that in addition to the various aspects of citizenry, we need Singaporeans to not only be IT-savvy but also be responsible digital citizens or digitizens.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: This pandemic has taught us how under-prepared many were for a global crisis that affected all countries.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: It has also brought to the forefront the need for digital acceleration and the importance of business continuity plans for businesses and organisations of all sizes.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, there is a vital need for a one-stop digital acceleration centre of excellence that can provide seamless solutions for companies and organisations seeking to ride the coming wave.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that MSF has plans to proactively reach out to these Singaporeans with a helping hand.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: It is timely and crucial to also include our seniors in our Digitalisation journey.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond family, friends and the wider community, our model of constantly creating public-private partnerships should not be forgotten.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On innovation, Harvard Business School professor Rosabeth Moss Kanter said, “Change is a threat when done to me, but an opportunity when done by me.” In my many conversations with fellow Singaporeans over the circuit breaker period, I have come to realise that many of them are embodying a key trait: adaptability through innovation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: When we announced the circuit breaker, we had to adapt to a completely new way of life.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Parents had to learn how to work from home while supervising their children in home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Teachers had to transition to teaching the entire syllabus online.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Businesses had to learn how to continue operating without access to their paper documents or any in person interaction.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: No one was spared from the need to change their way of life.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Out of this disorientation came the spirit of innovation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We have innovated by adopting video conferencing tools to conduct meetings and even marriages!

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our food establishments have innovated by serving their patrons without any physical interaction.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our civil servants had to innovate as well.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The SafeEntry declaration that I scanned today and the TraceTogether app which is running on my phone right now are all concrete examples of innovation driven by our teams at GovTech.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: It has exposed our fragilities and the urgent need to rethink our way forward.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The multi-faceted crisis the world is faced with did reveal itself in various ways in the last decades, continuously sending us signals on the urgent necessity to take action and embark on a transformational journey.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Throughout the history of humanity, crises have always represented critical junctures allowing mankind to take the path of innovation and positive transformation that contributed to building better societies.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We stand at the threshold of history to build a healthier, more peaceful, prosperous, inclusive, resilient and sustainable society in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, it behooves me to embrace the spirit of the Singapore Together Movement which has been labelled "a cornerstone" of nation building by Deputy Prime Minister as we beat the odds together.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This Budget provided what seemed to be a very generous sum of $5 billion to deal with the effects of COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: At this time, the number of cases in Singapore was less than 200 and the epicentre of the crisis was still very much in China, with the largest number of cases.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Within a month, the situation changed dramatically, as COVID-19 spread around the world, and became particularly rampant in Europe and the US, the number of cases in Singapore started spiking as well as we had more people return from overseas.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Government moved swiftly and Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Resilience Budget, which was what we needed in light of the worsening situation and the additional restrictions that the Government had to put in place to reduce the spread of the virus.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: As the number of cases continued to grow with more and more Singaporeans returning home, the danger of wide community spread emerged and the Government decided to implement the circuit breaker.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: To tide over the circuit breaker, Deputy Prime Minister announced a third Budget, the Solidarity Budget – solidarity because most Singaporeans, apart from our essential workers, stayed at home to prevent this crisis spreading.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Workplaces and schools closed and people tried to work from home while students engaged in home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: With the circuit breaker coming to an end, and with Singapore cautiously opening up, this latest Budget, is aptly named "Fortitude" and it aims to help get us moving once again in a very uncertain and volatile world.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Even as we have this debate today, the world is a different place.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Causeway, which used to see a little under half a million people a day cross up and down, is also quiet, allowing only vehicles with essential supplies coming through.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The largest number of COVID-19 cases now is in America, which also has an added crisis as the tragic death of George Lloyd has triggered a “Black Lives Matter” with large numbers of people on the street.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Singapore Government’s approach in this virus has been nimble.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We did not create this crisis, but we have to deal with the fallout.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We prioritised the saving of lives with a rigorous system of public messaging, contact tracing, quarantine and the expansion of medical resources.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Although we have one of the largest numbers of cases in Asia, which is partly because we have done very aggressive testing, we have managed to keep our fatality rates low because our medical capacity is adequate to provide for all who need it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Ministerial Task Force has communicated regularly, acted decisively and flexibly, staying calm and always having a clear plan for the situation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This Budget, the Fortitude Budget, is the latest additional spending the Government needs and I whole-heartedly support this.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Fortitude means courage in the face of adversity and that is exactly what Singapore needs to get back on its feet.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The earlier Budgets, particularly the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, helped businesses stay afloat during a time when Singapore and much of the world was frozen.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Our people retained jobs even though many were staying at home and were not able to work.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Those who were not so fortunate and lost jobs or income received immediate support.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This helped our people have resilience and solidarity.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Now, the time has come to slowly get back on our feet and move and this Budget again provides much needed lubrication to help this process.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: For businesses, the three main concerns are usually payroll, rental and financing.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Landlords in turn can get relief from their own mortgage obligations if they need it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: These well thought through schemes mitigate the three greatest concerns businesses will have and will, hopefully, give them fortitude to get up and get back in the game.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: For individuals, particularly those who have lost jobs or income, there is also significant help.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The biggest concern for individuals who are out of work is "Will we get more income?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And when will we get our next job?" This Budget provides for both apart from those with high incomes or higher value properties.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: These are exactly what we need during these difficult times.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This is significant, but it is also clear that this is not a decision the Government is taking lightly.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Based on what we know from MOF’s public data, the reserves managed by MAS are around $400 billion and Temasek has more than $300 billion on its balance sheet.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The full figure is, of course, bigger than this.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Back then we had a "V" shape recovery and the Government was able to pay back the draw-down within a year.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I do not expect the Government to be able to do so this time.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Yet, given the extraordinary situation we are in, I think this expenditure is well justified.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: (In Tamil):   This is a time of unprecedented challenges for the world from COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Many of our friends in other countries are facing unprecedented hardship and suffering, including being unable to find hospital beds and treatment when they need it and watching loved ones die without being able to be with them in their final moments or attend their funerals.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Now people’s main concern is their livelihoods, and that is exactly what this Budget addresses.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The aim is to help people get back on their feet and get their livelihoods back.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This Budget gives us "fortitude" to face the challenges ahead by helping to relieve the main things that cause us fear.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will commence the Sitting again at 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.59 pm until 4.20 pm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members have spent many hours raising many points, so it would not be possible for me to respond to each and every one of their points.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But where there are good ideas, the various Ministries will take them up and my various colleagues will address these later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In rounding up this debate, let me start by sharing my perspective on the nature of this crisis and the global and historical context.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is a global crisis of our generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Never before have we seen a global lockdown of this scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pandemic has exposed vulnerabilities in global supply chains, accelerated digitalisation and technological changes, and fragmented global markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is huge uncertainty on both the health and economic fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, it has opened up other fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The trigger of this crisis – the coronavirus – will continue to disrupt lives until a vaccine or suitable therapeutics are developed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are serious cascading effects on employment and people all over the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This comes amidst escalating geo-strategic competition between the US and China, which could destabilise the global order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is having a huge impact on the global economy because it shocked both the demand and supply side of the economy simultaneously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the demand side, reduced social interactions and weakened consumer confidence have significantly reduced consumption which, in turn, reduced income and investment levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the supply side, global lockdowns have disrupted deeply integrated supply chains across borders and slowed global trade and investment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These shocks reinforce each other and threaten to impair the long-term productive capacity of economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Measures that depend primarily on stimulating demand in the economy will not work due to supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Denise Phua and several other Members of Parliament asked about the global outlook.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The road to recovery will be long as we deal with persistent economic impact on workers, jobs and business.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond economic costs, there will be immense human and social costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The world took eight to 10 years following the Great Depression and global financial crisis to recover to pre-crisis unemployment levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should not be surprised that it takes as long, if not longer, to bounce back from the effects of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The First World War had a lasting impact on the employment prospects of a lost generation of youth in western economies, stripping them of a sense of hope and direction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is now talk of a global "lockdown generation" and fears that the youths of our time could have their skills, employability and incomes permanently affected even after the world recovers from the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must work to prevent a "COVID-19 generation" of workers and students in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All over the world, we have seen a Catch-22 situation developing as governments grapple with the tensions between saving lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The reluctance to freeze activities due to heavy economic losses has had tragic consequences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Delayed and incomplete measures to stem infections resulted in a massive number of casualties as healthcare systems were overwhelmed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore has managed to avert some of the harsher outcomes from COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We were able to act boldly as Singaporeans stood in unity, trusted the Government and worked together to save lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We imposed a prolonged circuit breaker to significantly reduce the community transmission rates over the past two months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We set up a joint task force to deal with the situation among our migrant worker community and the situation is improving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Aggressive testing and the professional dedication of our healthcare team have kept fatalities low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our battle against COVID-19 has reached an inflection point.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have now taken the first steps to reopen our economy safely, in a gradual and systematic way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now four days into our phased reopening.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to provide support for our workers and businesses to tide through this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Internationally, we are working to gradually reopen our borders safely with other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will allow for business travel, which is essential for our open economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Around the world, many countries have started to reopen and we are watching them closely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When infection cases slowed to a trickle, China started to reopen in late April, and South Korea, Germany and Japan relaxed their lockdown in May.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Infection rates rose for some countries that reopened earlier but they are actively managing the situation and working hard to respond to the new infections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are dealing with a highly infectious and agile virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must be psychologically prepared that infections could rise somewhat, even with the best precautionary measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are thus not reopening and going back to our familiar routines but into a new uncertain reality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans must learn and adapt to the new reality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must adjust to new norms, such as higher standards of personal and public hygiene, safe distancing and reduced social contact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will need to adjust to new ways of working, such as telecommuting, and acquire new skills relevant in the new economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Changing habits is difficult but we must all do our best.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Government interventions have become the cornerstone of the COVID-19 response as populations look towards the one institution that can organise and mobilise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Administrations, regardless of where they sit on the political spectrum or their belief in government intervention, have responded with substantial support packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have also stepped in to support distressed corporates from airlines to car makers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is more than double the size of our annual Budgets in preceding years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other words, we are looking to spend in one year what we would have done in two years or more in normal times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond the size of headline numbers, what matters even more is whether resources are directed to the right areas, to enable our people and our economy to rebound faster and stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The measures in our four Budgets have been designed to not only respond to the crisis but to also enable Singapore to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The measures aim to protect lives and livelihoods, deal with immediate concerns and build for our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Budgets aim to: (a) minimise the spread of the virus and risk to lives, which has largely been successful; (b) stabilise the economy, save jobs and viable companies, and protect livelihoods; (c) reposition workers, businesses and the community to respond to major shifts; and (d) seize new opportunities so as to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have put our people at the centre of our Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our measures on protecting livelihoods centre on helping people to stay employed and businesses to stay viable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fortunes of workers and businesses are intertwined.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By keeping the economy stable, we strengthen social resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our Labour Movement firmly believes – a job is the best welfare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The remaining goes to public health and social support measures, to supplement and strengthen the significant investments made and structural measures already in place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having set out the global context, let me now respond to the various issues raised in the Budget debate, under three broad themes: First, supporting jobs, livelihoods and our future economy; Second, maintaining a strong fiscal position; and Third, drawing on our deep reserves of social capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has, indeed, been the focus of our Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
