text: COVID-19 will take a lasting toll on the quantity and quality of jobs worldwide, despite countries' best efforts to mitigate the impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The International Labour Organisation has estimated that COVID-19 could raise global unemployment numbers by "far higher" than 25 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is worse than the 2009 Global Financial Crisis, which saw additional global unemployment of some 22 million workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For Singapore, the highest annual average number of unemployed residents on record was registered during the 2003 SARS epidemic, at 91,000 unemployed residents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The economic fallout of COVID-19 goes beyond unemployment numbers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even those who keep their jobs may suffer under-employment and significant income loss.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This could lead to a vicious cycle where income loss reduces consumption and affected businesses further reduce labour demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The human and social effects of unemployment and under-employment are no less debilitating.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For many of us, having a job means more than getting paid.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through our jobs, we are connected to the workings of the world and to other people, and we take pride in being a contributing member of society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At a personal level, losing a job can lead to a loss of identity, confidence and dignity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why, when COVID-19 struck, our top priority is to provide fiscal resources to help workers stay in their jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Jobs and Skills Package goes hand-in-hand with transformation in every business and at the industry level, through our Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every business that is confronted with structural changes and the shocks from COVID-19 will need to take a long hard look at its business model.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will need new markets, new products, or process innovations, and need to harness new technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They may need to work with their competitors as industries consolidate for scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that many of our business leaders understand more than ever we cannot take the "business as usual" or BAU attitude, or else there will be no business left.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New good jobs will be created in growth areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How do businesses get the right people into these re-designed or new jobs?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By hiring the right people and building up their skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fresh graduates or mid-career individuals with experience from other sectors are good choices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So are existing staff who can be re-skilled.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Business transformation, creating and sustaining good jobs need to be done as part of a coherent business and industry transformation plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dr Koh Poh Koon shared many examples of how the Labour Movement has partnered and supported businesses through their transformation journeys.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are three thrusts to our Jobs and Skills Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will save jobs in viable businesses and preserve workforce capability in sectors which are temporarily hard-hit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Close to two-thirds of these jobs are in our SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over $11 billion has already gone out to help employers defray wage costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to hear that many businesses have found the support useful and have factored it into their decision to retain jobs and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Jobs Support Scheme is what its name says clearly – it is meant to support jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are not supporting businesses for their own sakes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are supporting businesses – defraying their wage costs – so that they can retain and pay workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will open up pathways to new jobs across a range of skills levels and help local jobseekers of all ages and profiles to access them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Council had a productive first meeting just two days ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Again, I stress the effort we are making is unprecedented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also encourage our workers to step out of their comfort zone and acquire new skills to prepare for the structural changes ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Mr Goo Chong Kiat embarked on a Professional Conversion Programme (PCP) as a Senior Engineer with Systems on Silicon Manufacturing Company during the Circuit Breaker, as he wanted to deepen his skills in areas of Industry 4.0.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: His advice to others enrolling in PCPs is to keep an open mind and be ready to adapt to a dynamic environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we are dedicating additional help to groups which are harder hit, including our graduating students, our mid-career workers and self-employed persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Ang Hin Kee, Mr Desmond Choo, Ms Jessica Tan and Prof Lim Sun Sun have pointed out, we need concerted efforts to support these groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank Mr Pritam Singh for his support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad covered many of the initiatives in his speech earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our fresh job entrants will get enhanced access to jobs and traineeship opportunities in growth areas, through the TechSkills Accelerator programmes mentioned by Minister Iswaran yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our public agencies are also stepping up efforts to help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Muhammad Syabil Bin Mohamed Sazali is a fresh graduate from NUS Computer Engineering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This July, he will enroll in the Cyber Security Agency's 18-month Cybersecurity Development Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Syabil will be amongst the first batch of 40 officers to be groomed as cybersecurity professionals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With widespread digitalisation, demand for cybersecurity professionals will grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mature workers will receive strong support from the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and enhancements to the Adapt and Grow programmes introduced at the Unity Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Chew Kok Poh was an Operations Executive with ST Logistics for close to 19 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the deployment of Automated Guided Vehicles and a Warehouse Management System, his role was significantly transformed as a large portion of warehouse operation processes became automated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: ST Logistics leveraged the WSG redeployment PCP to upskill Kok Poh for the enhanced Logistics Executive role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He now works with the new automation systems to manage warehouse operations and conducts data analysis to plan their weekly manpower resources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I appreciate Mr Heng Chee How's support for our schemes to give our mature workers a leg up in the workplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now encouraging employers to re-design jobs as part of their broader enterprise transformation efforts through the Enterprise Development Grant, the Productivity Solutions Grant – Job Redesign, and the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many seniors can and want to work longer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to support them through the Senior Worker Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I join Minister Josephine Teo and Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng in thanking the many firms which have already stepped forward to play their part in supporting the creation of good job pathways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng also spoke about the support from NTUC FairPrice and Enterprise Groups, which have offered some 4,000 jobs and 300 traineeships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage more businesses to think long-term and continue to invest in people, or what economists call human capital development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Skilled workers make strong firms and strong firms create good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every business, every worker, must seek to maximise this synergy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But, despite our best efforts, we cannot possibly save every job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many sectors were already facing disruptions before COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For workers who are displaced, you have our assurance that if you make the effort, our tripartite partners will support you to tide through this difficulty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before COVID-19 struck, structural changes, such as the fragmentation of global supply chains and technological changes, were already in motion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we are fortunate that we started our structural transformation efforts early and companies that have made the efforts are adapting better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2015, we set up the Committee on the Future Economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Committee charted strategies to build our capacity for a vibrant, strong future economy and to create good opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some business leaders have told us that by embarking on transformation early, they have found it easier to pivot to new areas of opportunity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is Forefront Medical, a precision engineering firm providing manufacturing services to the medical industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Prior to COVID-19, Forefront Medical had started building up automation capabilities, adding cleanroom capacity and growing its local medtech talent pool.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These capabilities enabled the company to supply to more global medical companies when the pandemic struck.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has already secured a deal with one test kit company and is in discussion with two more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last week, I had an e-conference with a group of start-ups and venture funds in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The progress that they all have made in seizing new opportunities cheered me, including the safe bicycle helmet, 3D printing of instruments for swab tests and telemedicine.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the interest of time, let me just share a few more examples, to give a flavour of the progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And the first flavor is Shiok Meats, a start-up working to harvest crustacean meats from cells instead of animals, thereby eliminating the risk of food-borne diseases.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It aims to introduce these alternative proteins grown in food manufacturing facilities to restaurants in the next two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Novade provides smart field management software for the building and construction industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since COVID-19 struck, Novade has launched new functionalities to enable health monitoring procedures on work sites and is now helping clients use these functions to restart and carry out operations safely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: ViSenze specialises in retail AI solutions, including virtual try-outs of products using a real-time camera recognition function.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been piloting these new technologies with retailers to get ready for a "new normal" in post-COVID-19 shopping and is now doubling down its efforts to help retail clients worldwide transform their operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The start-up mantra is to disrupt the world, to make it better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But with COVID-19 disrupting the world, it is good to see start-ups pivoting to enabling us to cope better with a disrupted world, with the right innovations!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the face of the deep uncertainties that confront the world today, what must Singapore do to survive and succeed?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The post-COVID-19 world will be different from today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We may not know the exact contours of how this world will look like, but we know the forces that are shaping it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Emerging Stronger Task Force, led by Minister Desmond Lee and PSA International Group CEO Tan Chong Meng, are studying key shifts and developing recommendations in the areas of technology and innovation, digitalisation and disruption to global supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the course of its work, the Task force will consult multiple stakeholders and draw on insights beyond its membership, so that their findings and recommendations are relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Members spoke about the need to respond quickly to the structural shifts, and I thank Members, including Mr Ang Wei Neng, Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Douglas Foo for their insights.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Accelerating our economic transformation is indeed a national priority and both workers and employers must do their part to stay focused on this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Iswaran sets out clearly that this crisis has crystallised the need and opportunity for digitalisation and we can only emerge stronger by making a decisive push towards a digital future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as Mr Christopher de Souza puts it, riding this wave of digitalisation is key to ensuring that our Singaporeans are ready for borderless job opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will also be a premium on resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Arasu Duraisamy, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Saktiandi Supaat pointed out, one way for businesses to build resilience, is to build up a strong Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will not only create opportunities for our local workers but also help our businesses continue to operate sustainably even as other economies grow and develop, or even if there are disruptions to external labour supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our next phase of growth, we must anchor Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like a pearl that is part of a strand of vital global nodes across the world, we must play a valued and inextricable role in the new global configuration.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will do so by forging new partnerships and bringing new value to the world through innovation and deep capabilities, including technological capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am bringing together the work of our Future Economy Council and the Research, Innovation and Enterprise Council to do so, by enabling our industry clusters to harness the rich opportunities catalysed by innovation networks and the creation of new scientific knowledge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as Assoc Prof Walter Theseira said, we must undertake this great exercise of economic restructuring together, as equal partners and as one people, in the creation of a new Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 situation is a mighty storm that has damaged sails and forced ships around the world to go into harbour.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While waiting for the storm to subside, we must make the best use of this downtime to build new strengths and capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us take this rare chance to repair, upgrade our ship and install new instruments, re-orientate our mental compass and strengthen our sailors, so that when the fair wind comes, we will sail out faster and further than ever before.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is what our four Budgets enable us to do – let us make the best use of these!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have explained our immediate priorities to support jobs and livelihoods and why we need to accelerate transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our strong response is projected to stabilise economic activity during this difficult period, and position Singapore for recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is very significant because when you have a higher base, future growth, even at the same percentage rate, means that you reach a higher level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Alex Yam mentioned, some are of the view that we have spent too much, while others think it is too little.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These contrasting views show that crisis budgeting is anything but straightforward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These decisions have been made after careful deliberations, based on the best information available at that time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the COVID-19 situation develops, we have continued to enhance and refine our schemes, as evidenced by our four Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even then, let us stay vigilant – as I said at the outset, we are facing unprecedented levels of uncertainty across various fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such contingency budgeting reflects both the unprecedented levels of severity, as well as uncertainty, of this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang asked if the Government can provide an indication of how the Funds may potentially be used.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As designed, the Contingencies Funds can be drawn upon if there is a need to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as designed, we have not designated specific purposes for the Funds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In sizing it, we have run some "what if" scenarios, including the possibility that we may experience a setback in our fight against COVID-19 or the global economy does much worse than currently expected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, unlike our usual annual Budget, where we seek to provide as much details as possible, we are setting aside a sum to meet future events or circumstances that are possible, but for which we cannot yet predict with certainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is indeed a special feature that allow us to respond swiftly to unforeseen developments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the governance around the use of Contingencies Funds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The use of Contingencies Funds is not new.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With greater uncertainty, it is natural for us to cater for a bigger quantum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Constitution includes safeguards over its use.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, these drawdowns must be replaced through a subsequent Supplementary Supply Bill or a Final Supply Bill that have to be presented to and voted on by Parliament before seeking President's assent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This provides additional checks and balances over new spending from the Contingencies Funds will continue to ensure judicious use of the Contingencies Funds for urgent and unforeseen needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the uncertainty subsides, we can reduce the amount set aside in the Contingencies Funds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members have also pointed out another exceptional feature of our Budgets this Financial Year – the draw on Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For most countries, borrowing is the only way to fund their largest stimulus packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This increases the risk of unsustainable debt financing, which has severe consequences for the economy in the long run.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Countries that have taken on significant additional debt to pay for their support measures will have to find new ways to repay their debt and interest accrued.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Future generations will be required to shoulder this debt, be it in the form of higher taxes, higher inflation, or lower returns on their retirement assets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Future generations will also be affected in other ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In order to service debt repayment, there will be less fiscal room to invest in human capital or infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The "Lockdown Generation" in these countries will end up paying for this crisis a long way down the road.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are fortunate that in this hour of crisis, we have our national reserves to depend on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves allow us to deal with this crisis from a position of strength and give us options in a period of uncertainty like this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Vikram Nair likened our reserves to a "Golden Goose", painstakingly built up since our Independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Murali Pillai have pointed out, our reserves are our key strategic advantage in the current environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, it assures Singaporeans that we have the means to navigate the challenges ahead, to protect our lives and to sustain our livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, it fosters confidence in global investors, that our economic fundamentals are sound and stable in the long term and that we have enough resources to emerge stronger from the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, it protects us during this period of flux.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Detractors and speculators know well enough not to take advantage of this crisis, to attack our economy or currency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We did not get here by chance or good fortune.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have designed and implemented policies that discourage waste or over-consumption.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have run our public services based on outcomes, not on size of spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, we are in this fortunate position because of consistent hard work, prudence, long-term planning and discipline of those who came before us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such prudence and discipline are not always appreciated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have had vigorous debates in this House, on whether the Government could afford to spend more freely from reserves, instead of running Budget surpluses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as recently as January this year, before the Unity Budget was unveiled, many commentators inside and outside of this House speculated on how large our accumulated reserves would be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The total of our four Budgets, including the COVID-19 packages, is more than double the size of our annual Budgets in preceding years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our reserves are a limited resource and we must not take them for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We owe it to our people – seniors, middle-aged, young and those yet to be born – to be prudent and ensure good governance, so that they too have the resources to navigate future challenges in an uncertain world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government put back into the Past Reserves the $4 billion it had earlier drawn on in 2009, during the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And not a single cent of the $150 billion of reserves that backed the Government's guarantee of bank deposits was used, when our banking system emerged safely from the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This current crisis is of a significantly larger scale and reach than the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are facing huge uncertainties regarding the course of the pandemic and its economic and social implications.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, how long would it take to build this back?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At this moment, we must focus our minds fully on making the best use of the resources that we have deployed, be prepared to work hard in the years to come, and have the resolve to rebuild our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, the Singapore economy can emerge stronger, and we will be in a strong position to build up our resources.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But rest assured that we are committed to rebuild not just our reserves, but also to continue developing Singaporeans and building Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Muhd Faisal Manap and Mr Dennis Tan asked if the President was given information on the amount available in the reserves when the Government sought her in-principle support for drawing on them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am surprised that both Mr Faisal and Mr Dennis Tan had to ask.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is public information that, under our Constitution, the President has access to information about the size of reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under Article 22F of the Constitution, in the exercise of her functions under the Constitution, the President is entitled to any information regarding the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, on the MOF website, it is already mentioned that the President has full information about the size of the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the process of seeking President's approval, the Government has conducted two briefings to President and the Council of Presidential Advisers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These briefings covered the Government's assessment of the global and local health and economic situations, the details of the measures and the resources needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministers Gan Kim Yong, Chan Chun Sing, Lawrence Wong and Indranee Rajah were with me.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our system, the President is the custodian of our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She needs to concur with any draw, and her decision is made in full knowledge of why the draw is necessary, and the size of our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, Members have heard the President's message in the Resilience Budget, delivered on her behalf by the Speaker, just before my Ministerial Statement then.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have a strict governance system, scrupulously observed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have also asked why the Government does not reveal the size of the reserves and let the public decide if we should use more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I had explained this to Members of this House during my last round-up speech in early April – it is not in our national interest to reveal the full size of our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides being a buffer against crisis and providing investment return to supplement our annual Budget, our reserves also form our strategic defence against threats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as a strategic asset, we would be diminishing its value if we disclose this for potential adversaries to use against us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No responsible leader will lay bare your nation's defence plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fiscal discipline is one of the fundamental principles underpinning Singapore's fiscal system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We spend prudently within our means and responsibly with a value-for-money culture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rule to run balanced Budgets for each term of Government remains relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also spend equitably, with the principle that each generation bears the cost of the benefits that they enjoy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is why we do not borrow to fund our recurrent spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Doing so means getting our children to fund our current spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will be less resources for our children, after repaying such debt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While interest rates may be low now, there is no certainty that we will be able to repay accumulated debt obligations in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is especially so with the uncertain economic outlook, where all countries, including Singapore, will be operating in a tighter fiscal space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we have good reasons not to borrow for our current expenditure, the Government is already using debt productively and equitably to generate long-term returns for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, to develop the domestic debt market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The borrowing proceeds are invested and we are able to cover the debt servicing costs through the investment returns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, we leverage the strength of the Government's balance sheet to reduce borrowing costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The debt repayments will be made during a period when the airport will be generating economic returns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lastly, as I had also mentioned in Budget 2019, the Government is considering borrowing for major long-term infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Long-term infrastructure requires hefty upfront investments and the costs are lumpy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But once built, they benefit many generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Borrowing for such developments allows us to spread costs equitably across current and future generations, without the need for sharp increases in taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have done so in the past, we borrow for many worthwhile investments that have benefited several generations such as the first terminal at Changi Airport and our first MRT lines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will continue to generate growth for future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that Members of Parliament have raised concerns about the sustainability of tapping on the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked whether we are leaving enough reserves behind for future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Mohd Irshad asked how the draw would influence our policies, moving forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The crisis has underscored the importance of upholding the prudence and discipline of our forefathers to spend responsibly, and prepare for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why, even as we devote considerable resources to overcome the immediate challenges posed by COVID-19, we must continue to plan ahead to secure a fiscally sustainable future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the medium to long term, our structural needs will persist, and significant fiscal outlay will be required.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to continue investing in healthcare, education and training, and infrastructure, so that we have adequate capacity to take care of our seniors and support an ageing population; so that we give every child a good start, and give every Singaporean the opportunity to re-skill and up-skill to access good jobs, and so that Singapore remains a liveable city and a place we are proud to call home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These heavy and rising expenditures were known even before the outbreak of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has increased the urgency for some of these investments, such as developing advanced medical research and production capabilities, and expanding training capacity for our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is hence critical that we deploy the right mix of fiscal instruments that meets our principles of prudence and equitable spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I mentioned earlier, major long-term infrastructure spending, which requires hefty upfront investments but benefits many generations of Singaporeans, may be financed through borrowing to fairly distribute the cost among those who benefit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the other hand, recurrent spending, should be met with recurrent revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such spending primarily benefits the current generation of Singaporeans, and so, it is fair and responsible for all of us to do our part and chip in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the GST rate increase does take place, we will cushion the impact for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to absorb GST on publicly-subsidised healthcare and education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, our taxes and transfers system will remain fair and progressive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this differentiated and principled fiscal strategy, each generation rightly pays for the benefits that they enjoy, and we do not saddle future generations with our bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is an equitable approach, and will continue to be the cornerstone of fiscal sustainability for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I announced it in the last week of the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we debate the Budget a few days into Phase One of our reopening.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Fortitude Budget supports us as we gradually re-open our society and economy, braces us for the difficult months ahead, and prepares us to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During this time, I have seen and felt Singaporeans' fortitude in action.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been driven and inspired by the fortitude of our people and companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Christopher de Souza said, it is about courage in adversity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is forged in crises past, and hardened in crises present.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It comes from the strength of mind and character.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the case of Singapore, our fortitude comes too from the strength of our reserves – the financial reserves that I have just spoken about, and just as important, our deep reserves of social capital.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our social capital is made up of the intangible bonds that unite our multi-racial society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The bonds of trust among ourselves and between people and the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our national conversations on the Singapore we want to build.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is the spirit of Singapore Together, where all parts of society work together in partnership, keeping us strong and united, even as the pandemic fragments many societies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Josephine Teo and Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng shared how our tripartite structure acts to build fortitude in our workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This crisis has brought out the best in our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans have come together to donate their Solidarity Payments to charitable causes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over 10,000 people have stepped forward over the past two months to volunteer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They run errands for seniors living alone, distribute care packs, manage the National Care Hotline and deliver food supplies to migrant workers and vulnerable families, among others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, during his in-camp training, Mr Rajasegaran Ramachandran stepped up to serve at the frontline as a medic at the Singapore Expo care facility to care for COVID-19 patients as he wanted to do his part for the nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Corporates, volunteer centres and community groups have also come together to contribute.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And there are many encouraging stories of people helping one another, such as seniors providing mutual support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Individuals, too, have shown resilience and adapted to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Catherine Tang, who has mild autism and works at The Art Faculty store at the Enabling Village, attended online courses during the circuit breaker to improve her customer service skills and support the store's e-commerce platform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is good to see her keeping so cheerful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many public servants across different agencies have been working hard during COVID-19 to help Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They coordinate our pandemic response, respond to Singaporeans' queries, implement support measures and keep up regular Government services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many more have stepped up to take on frontline roles such as safe distancing ambassadors to help keep our communities safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every constructive action adds to our social reserves that allow us to face this challenge with fortitude.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage more Singaporeans to step forward and help one another in our community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, contrary to what Mr Singh has mentioned earlier that we are only consulting people inside the business community, the Government has taken extra effort to take a far broader approach.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I think yesterday, Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about Our Singapore Conversation and Singapore Together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just last week, Ministers Desmond Lee, Grace Fu, Indranee Rajah and I had a very good discussion with leaders in our social service agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We all felt very cheered by the dedication of our people in the frontline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They were doing their utmost to support our vulnerable people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a great example of democracy of deed – of taking action to make a difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And Ms Yip Pin Xiu mentioned about the sports community and how they are supporting one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In growing our social reserves, we must continue to support and care for those who have less and those who have fallen on hard times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will walk this journey with you and leave no one behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the last two days, Members of Parliament like Mr Ang Hin Kee, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Ms Sylvia Lim, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Louis Ng proposed refinements and additional measures for various groups in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In coming out with each of the Budgets, my colleagues and I had reached out through many channels – social service agencies, community partners, unionists and grassroots leaders – to identify where the greatest needs are.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We then carefully considered how we can help those who are most in need, especially those among us who are less able to articulate their needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The result is not perfect but has gone a long way in alleviating pain points.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari, Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Anthea Ong asked if we can enhance existing COVID-19 support schemes for low-income workers and households, especially if unemployment persists.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While some COVID-19 schemes such as the Solidarity Payment and Solidarity Utilities Credit cover all Singaporeans, the overall payouts are tilted towards lower- to middle-income groups as they have less to fall back on in difficult times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There may be instances of families who marginally miss the eligibility criteria but also need help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will assess these on a case-by-case basis, and refine our schemes as the situation develops.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other Members like Miss Cheng Li Hui, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Sylvia Lim raised concerns on how some Singaporeans may feel marginalised by the rapid adoption of digital technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Iswaran laid out our road map for a digital future, with digital inclusion at the heart of our plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: New initiatives like the SG Digital Office, Hawkers Go Digital and Seniors Go Digital will complement existing programmes such as NEU PC Plus and Home Access.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We take your concerns like the need to equip our seniors with cybersecurity awareness seriously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we should not let fear paralyse us into sticking with the status quo.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the world changes, we want to move fast on digital transformation but more importantly, we are determined to move together in digital inclusion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Denise Phua, Ms Yip Pin Xiu and Mr Melvin Yong also called for more support for vulnerable groups, including those with special needs and mental health conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Denise Phua has made a thoughtful suggestion – or several suggestions, including one to formalise a workstream on employment for people with disabilities within the National Jobs Council.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have just spoken to Senior Minister Tharman and, in fact, both of us welcome her leadership on this and are glad to support her proposal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with our community partners, we have put in resources – finances, networks and systems – over the years to support the vulnerable and I assure members that we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we have built up physical networks to strengthen social service delivery through the SG Cares Community Network.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such physical links are complemented with digital ones to build up bonds among people and within the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: WE CARE Community Services set up a cloud-based contact centre and tele-counselling facilities so that staff can take calls from their homes to continue serving persons with addiction issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This approach increased participation rates among its beneficiaries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, the COVID-19 support measures should be seen in the context of the larger suite of measures to protect jobs and livelihoods and support our businesses during this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some people have said that the support for jobs is big while the support to me or my household seems small.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A thoughtful commentator said to me, it is right that the Government has devoted, as a central plank of the four Budgets, this central focus on supporting our workers to retain their jobs or to move into new jobs, because should the sole breadwinner of the family lose his or her job, the effect on the whole family is much more adverse.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, it is important that we see this in totality, not just what is in each little compartment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Moreover, bear in mind that our social spending has nearly doubled over the last ten years and this reflects our commitment to invest in and support our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Terence Ho and Ms Yip Pin Xiu spoke on areas that merit additional support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will take lessons from COVID-19 to continue refining our social support policies to help build stronger families and communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Individuals and the community too play a role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan said, "the Government can act as a catalyst but we ourselves must be the change makers." There is a role for every Singaporean to play.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have the reserves of strength and kindness in each of us to pay it forward in deed or resources to help support someone else.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Moments of crisis are a test of the strength of our reserves and we have the strength – not least of all in ourselves as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have the fortitude to each do our part and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   Today is the fourth day of the post-circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have entered the first phase of resuming work and school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we are unable to predict how the COVID-19 situation will evolve, we will need to remain vigilant and observe safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the past few months, the global economy has been badly hit in terms of demand and supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small and open economy, Singapore has also been severely affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In four months, we have introduced four Budgets totaling around $100 billion to deal with the COVID-19 situation to protect our health, save jobs, save livelihoods, save businesses and secure our future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Budget not only protects us during the storm and acts as a buffer during the current crisis, it is also a booster that will drive the economy when the storm passes and will help Singaporeans and businesses prepare for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The tripartite partners will continue to work closely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is one of the key factors that will help us overcome the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, we should not believe that every job will be saved or all companies will be able to continue operating.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those who are badly hit by COVID-19 and those who need to make structural changes will have to overhaul their business strategies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, through various measures complemented by various industry transformation road maps, we will speed up the pace of economic transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other countries, governments have issued debt to finance their relief measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is different, because Singaporeans from previous generations and previous governments have been managing our finances prudently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will use every dollar wisely so that the economy can recover swiftly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the future, we are determined to rebuild our economy and work hard for our next generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also need to continue to manage our finances prudently, increase our income through sustainable avenues to meet the needs of recurrent expenditures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be prepared for the new normal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 situation has worsened the impact of economic cycles, sped up structural changes in the global economy and deepened the fault-lines between countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digitalisation of the economy will be deeper, broader and faster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Market structures, trade flows, people and capital flows will also be affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore will continue to strengthen trade and economic links with other countries to stabilise our supply chains and trade networks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies must move with the times in order to seize opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Workers must also upskill and be willing to take on new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 situation has also highlighted the challenges faced by people in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, it is encouraging that Singaporeans have shown their best during this period, for example, cohesion, empathy, and helping those around us who are in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope Singaporeans will continue to show care for others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also hope that through the Singapore Together movement, we will be able to create a more inclusive and caring society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is undoubtedly the most serious challenge faced by our generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The First World War resulted in a "lost" generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Internationally, there are also discussions on whether lockdowns due to COVID-19 will lead to a "lockdown" generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly believe that Singapore has the capability to overcome the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as we work together, stay united and resilient, forge ahead with fortitude, there will be no "lockdown" generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, we will emerge stronger and become a generation that is more united, stronger and more resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I will now conclude in English.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the start of the speech, I spoke of the great uncertainty ahead and the fundamental shifts that are taking place at an accelerated pace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What does this changed world demand of us?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to adapt and transform ourselves – with agility, creativity and determination.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To survive and emerge stronger from the huge uncertainties ahead, we must get three things right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we must have good governance and strong, adaptive leadership – a Government that works with you and for you; that is always honest with our people about the truth; steadfast in preparing and anticipating what lies ahead; and committed to supporting our people and businesses to meet uncertainty head-on and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must have strong social reserves, not just in each of us as individuals or just in our different communities, but across all levels and parts of our society, working together and holding one another up with trust and in solidarity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must be crystal clear and unwavering about our values and mission – what we stand for and what we are here to achieve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These make up the essence of the Singapore Together movement, which I launched last year to take Singapore forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than ever before, these fundamentals will be crucial as we navigate the uncertainties ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our circumstances have changed over the years, but the Government's aspirations for Singapore have not.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is to be a place where our people, regardless of race, language or religion, can build a better life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We seek to be a vibrant and innovative economy, so as to create good jobs and opportunities for our people; a smart, green, healthy and liveable city that we can be proud to call home; a fair, just and harmonious society where our people care for and support one another; and a safe and secure nation, and a responsible member of the global community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is not the first crisis that Singapore has faced nor will it be the last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Past generations of Singaporeans have weathered numerous challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Pioneer Generation survived the hardships of World War II.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation grew up in a tumultuous period leading up to Singapore's Independence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How will we respond to this crisis of our generation?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The one constant is how we have persevered with fortitude and emerged stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This time, there will be huge uncertainties ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we will continue to persevere and we will, once again, emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are fighting this battle from a position of strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We stand together as one united country and one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are uniquely fortunate to have built up a priceless harmony, sense of common identity and shared destiny, even as we draw on our diversity of strengths and experiences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will never allow a crisis to bring us down.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even in these trying times, we continue to look ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people are hardworking and disciplined, willing to learn new skills and adapt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have enterprising businesses that are ready to grasp new opportunities and thrive in the face of competition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We stand in solidarity with, and care for and support, one another, especially the more vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people, businesses, the Labour Movement and the Government stand together in partnership, not in division.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We stand in solidarity with countries around the world in this pandemic, building on our assets of trust, reliability and efficiency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have the grit to persevere in adversity with fortitude.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will forge new paths and never waver in our efforts to build a stronger Singapore together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have highly dedicated frontline workers who have worked day and night over the last few months to keep us safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will overcome this crisis with fortitude and solidarity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am surprised that Mr Faisal Manap did not hear this statement of mine so clearly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is in our Constitution and it is on the website of MOF.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As I have said at the outset, all Members of this House have spoken extensively on this Budget and if I were to cover every single point, we would go beyond these two hours.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But rest assured that whatever good suggestions will be taken up by the various Ministries so that we can respond to each of these.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Pursuant to Standing Order 44(2), the Motion to consider the Ministerial Statement on the Government's Plans in Our Continuing Fight Against COVID-19 Pandemic lapses at the conclusion of the debate.
